prompt:
Use case: ads-marketing
Asset type: wide Shopify homepage conversion-section background, approximately 3:2 landscape (1536×1024-ish)
Primary request: Create a decorative vintage candy-shop sales-counter backdrop designed to sit behind real HTML product cards and conversion copy.
Scene/backdrop: Frontal, straight-on view of a handsome honey-oak shop counter spanning the lower portion of the frame, with aged cream paper-plaster walls behind it. Include only two small glass sweet jars, positioned near the far left and far right edges so they never compete with the center.
Subject: The empty counter stage and softly aged candy-shop interior atmosphere; no merchandise display in the center.
Style/medium: Premium hand-crafted photographic realism with subtle vintage theatrical set-design character, tactile natural materials, refined commercial art direction, believable patina, not kitsch.
Composition/framing: Wide landscape, symmetrical frontal viewpoint, generous large clean center area, ample usable negative space across the middle and upper-middle for overlaid HTML product cards and copy. Edge decorations must remain small and peripheral. Keep the central counter surface open, calm, and uncluttered. No shallow crop that cuts away the usable counter.
Lighting/mood: Gentle theatrical spotlight centered softly on the clean stage area, warm ambient falloff, subtle depth, inviting and premium, with restrained contrast so foreground HTML remains legible.
Color palette: Warm honey oak and aged cream, restrained muted accents of vintage red, deep teal, and antique gold only at the far periphery.
Materials/textures: Fine oak grain, softly worn cream paper-plaster, clear glass jars with a small amount of generic unwrapped colorful sweets, understated aged brass details.
Text (verbatim): ""
Constraints: Background-only asset for a conversion section; leave the center visually quiet and empty; exactly two small glass sweet jars near the far edges; premium hand-crafted realism; straight-on frontal perspective; no central objects.
Avoid: phones, phone cases, electronic devices, people, hands, faces, logos, brands, text, letters, numbers, typography, signage, labels, watermarks, ribbons, bows, sale badges, discount graphics, price tags, claims, product cards, UI, posters, packaging, central props, excessive clutter, oversaturated colors, cartoon style.
